content: I'll read the test image to analyze the disease symptoms.

**Observations from the image:**

- **Affected part:** Banana fruits (post-harvest)
- **Key features:**
  - The leftmost banana shows extensive dark brown to black irregular lesions covering a large portion of the fruit surface
  - Scattered smaller brown/dark spots are also visible on the adjacent yellow bananas
  - The lesions appear sunken and coalescing on the most affected fruit
  - Discoloration pattern is irregular, not confined to a single end
  - Other fruits are at various ripening stages with scattered spot lesions beginning to develop

**Disease matching:**

- **Anthracnose** (*Colletotrichum musae*): Post-harvest fruit disease presenting as dark sunken lesions that expand and coalesce on the fruit surface — matches the image very well.
- **Cigar End Rot**: Dry rot confined primarily to the blossom/distal tip only — the lesions here are too widespread to fit.
- **Cordana Leaf Spot, Yellow/Black Sigatoka, Panama Disease**: All primarily affect leaves or vascular tissue, not fruit surfaces — ruled out.
- **Bunchy Top**: Viral, affects whole plant architecture — ruled out.

The widespread dark, irregular, coalescing lesions on the fruit surface affecting multiple bananas at various stages is classic for **Anthracnose**.
